newsitem.title: NORWAY: UBN announces cost cuts, staff reduction.
newsitem.headline: UBN announces cost cuts, staff reduction.

text.p: Union Bank of Norway (UBN), Norway's biggest savings bank, said on Thursday it would cut costs by an annual 200 million crowns from the year 2000 by reducing personnel and introducing new technology.
The bank did not say what the cost effects would be in the years leading up to 2000.

"It will depend on a series of things such as the introduction of new technology, new work methods, organisational changes and other things that will be phased in at different times," a UBN spokesman told Reuters.

A statement said the bank, which now has 3,233 employees, would reduce staff by 450 people in the next few years. It said 155 million crowns were being set aside in the 1996 accounts to handle costs in connection with the reductions.
Sweeping cost cuts were announced last year by Norway's top commercial banks, Den norske Bank (DnB) and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse.
